labs.title: Create and share a Power BI report from a semantic model
labs.summary: Explore a star-schema semantic model, build a two-page Power BI report with appropriate visuals, save it, verify it, and share with least privilege.
labs.scenario: Tailwind Traders has a certified **Sales** semantic model in the Power BI service and managers need both an executive overview and product detail page. In the **simulated Power BI experience** on your lab VM, review the star-schema model, create a report with KPI, comparison, trend, slicer, and detail visuals, save it as **Regional sales**, run a final verification check, and share it with **Sales managers** using read-only permissions.
learningObjectives: Explain the role of a Power BI semantic model and star-schema relationships
Choose visual types that fit KPI, comparison, trend, detail, and filtering tasks
Create multiple report pages from one governed semantic model
Share a report with least-privilege permissions
prerequisites: Know basic chart types and measures

modelTables.name: Sales
modelTables.fields: DateKey, ProductKey, Region, Quantity, Total Sales

steps.title: Open the Sales semantic model
steps.instruction: Select **Workspaces**, open **Sales Analytics**, and then open the **Sales** semantic model.
steps.hint: The model type is shown in the Items list.
steps.explanation: A semantic model provides governed fields, measures, relationships, and security for reports.

rules.description: The Sales semantic model was opened

steps.title: Review tables and relationships
steps.instruction: Review the **Tables** and **Relationships** lists. Confirm that **Sales** is a fact table related to **Product** and **Date** dimensions, then select **Create report**.
steps.hint: Reports use the model relationships when visuals combine fields from multiple tables.
steps.explanation: Measures such as Total Sales are evaluated through the semantic model, so visuals stay consistent across reports.

steps.title: Add four appropriate visuals
steps.instruction: Add these visuals: **Card** with **Sales[Total Sales] measure**, **Clustered column chart** with **Sales[Region]** and **Sales[Total Sales] measure**, **Line chart** with **Date[Month]** and **Sales[Total Sales] measure**, and **Slicer** with **Date[Year]**.
steps.hint: Use a card for one KPI, a column chart for category comparison, a line chart for a time trend, and a slicer for filtering. A pie chart is not a good trend visual, and a table is not a KPI card.
steps.explanation: Choosing the right visual type helps the report answer the business question quickly and accurately.

rules.failureFeedback: Add a Card using the Total Sales measure.

rules.description: Clustered column chart shows Sales by Region
rules.failureFeedback: Add a Clustered column chart with Region and Total Sales.

rules.description: Line chart shows Sales by Month
rules.failureFeedback: Add a Line chart with Month and Total Sales.

steps.title: Add the Product detail page visual
steps.instruction: Add a **Table** for **Product detail page matrix** using **Product[Category]** and **Sales[Total Sales] measure**.
steps.hint: A table is useful when managers need exact detail rows; charts are better for comparisons and trends.
steps.explanation: A second report page can provide detail while the overview stays focused on KPIs and trends. Both pages reuse the same semantic model.

rules.failureFeedback: Add the product detail Table with Category and Total Sales.

steps.title: Save the report
steps.instruction: Select **Save** and save the report as **Regional sales** in **Sales Analytics**.
steps.hint: Save only after all four visuals are present on the canvas.
steps.explanation: Saving creates a report item in the workspace while the semantic model remains the shared data source.

rules.failureFeedback: Save the report as Regional sales in Sales Analytics.

steps.title: Verify the report before sharing
steps.instruction: After saving, complete **Final verification** with **Overview and Product detail**, **Sales semantic model**, and **Year slicer filters visuals** turned on.
steps.hint: Verification catches reports that accidentally use a static export or only a single page.
steps.explanation: A final check confirms the report uses the governed semantic model and that interactive filters support self-service analysis.

steps.title: Share with least privilege
steps.instruction: Share **Regional sales** with **Sales managers** using **Read** permission. Leave **Allow recipients to build content with the data associated with this report** off.
steps.hint: Build permission is for users who need to create new reports from the semantic model.
steps.explanation: Least privilege gives report consumers the access they need without allowing them to edit the report or build new content from the model.

labs.solution:
1. Select **Workspaces**, open **Sales Analytics**, then open the **Sales** semantic model.
2. Review **Tables** and **Relationships**: Sales relates to Product and Date, and the model exposes the Total Sales measure.
3. Select **Create report**. Add a **Card** with **Sales[Total Sales] measure**.
4. Add a **Clustered column chart** with **Sales[Region]** and **Sales[Total Sales] measure**.
5. Add a **Line chart** with **Date[Month]** and **Sales[Total Sales] measure**.
6. Add a **Slicer** with **Date[Year]**.
7. Add a **Table** for **Product detail page matrix** with **Product[Category]** and **Sales[Total Sales] measure**.
8. Select **Save** and save as `Regional sales` in **Sales Analytics**.
9. Complete **Final verification** with **Overview and Product detail**, **Sales semantic model**, and Year slicer interactions on.
10. Select **Share**. Share with **Sales managers**, permission **Read**, and leave **Allow recipients to build content with the data associated with this report** off.
